terms.register: vōx cōmica et poētica: Plaut., Enn.; Verg., Hor.
evidence: Plaut. Men. 834: Concēde hūc, mea nāta
Plaut. Pers. 332: sequere hāc, mea gnāta, mē
terms.comment: The participle of nāscor as a noun, like nātus, son; comedy keeps the old gn-.

phrases.latin: Concēde hūc, mea nāta, ab istōc quam potest longissimē.
phrases.english: Come over here, my daughter, as far away from him as you can.

sources: The grouped card gave no source for this word.
